title: Strong thin-tree conjecture
aliases: Strong form of Goddyn's thin-tree conjecture
decision_reason: Explicit strong all-cuts formulation and independent corroboration; current literature and full relevant partial-result statements reviewed; duplicate and separated A35 adversarial checks passed. Accepted as a research draft awaiting batch integration.

problem_fingerprint.model_or_objects: Finite undirected unweighted loopless multigraph G=(V,E); parallel edges are distinct and counted with multiplicity. A spanning tree T is a subset of its edges.
problem_fingerprint.domain: All such multigraphs, without planarity, genus, transitivity or prescribed-cut-family restrictions.
problem_fingerprint.regularity_and_data_class: No numerical edge weights or costs; no spectral assumption.
problem_fingerprint.boundary_or_initial_conditions: For every nonempty proper vertex set S, delta_G(S) consists of edges with exactly one endpoint in S.
problem_fingerprint.parameter_range: Every positive integer k; G is k-edge-connected, meaning each nontrivial cut has at least k edges.
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: There exists one finite absolute constant C>0 such that for every k and every eligible G there exists one spanning tree T satisfying the bound simultaneously for every nontrivial cut S.
problem_fingerprint.normalization: Unweighted edge counts, with multiplicity. The constant is independent of graph size, connectivity, graph and cut.
problem_fingerprint.observable_or_norm: max over nontrivial S of |T intersect delta_G(S)|/|delta_G(S)|.
problem_fingerprint.limit_regime_and_order: Uniform finite-graph assertion; no probabilistic or thermodynamic limit.
problem_fingerprint.requested_conclusion: |T intersect delta_G(S)| <= (C/k)|delta_G(S)| for all nontrivial S.
problem_fingerprint.computational_model_and_dependencies: Existence only; no polynomial runtime, efficient certificate or assumption such as P != NP.

applied_significance: A connected network backbone should use only a controlled fraction of every cut's available links. Strong thinness would guarantee such a tree uniformly in network size; for k>C removing it retains edge connectivity at least k-C. It also provides a route to rounding directed routing relaxations, with existence and efficient construction supplying different guarantees.

proposed_statement_text:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite undirected loopless multigraph with at least two vertices. Parallel edges are counted separately. For a nonempty proper set $S\subsetneq V$, write $\delta_G(S)$ for the edges with exactly one endpoint in $S$. For an integer $k\ge1$, call $G$ $k$-edge-connected if $|\delta_G(S)|\ge k$ for every such $S$.

Does there exist an absolute constant $C>0$ such that every $k$-edge-connected $G$, for every $k\ge1$, has a spanning tree $T\subseteq E$ satisfying

$$
|T\cap\delta_G(S)|\le\frac{C}{k}\,|\delta_G(S)|
\qquad\text{for every }\varnothing\ne S\subsetneq V?
$$

The same tree must satisfy every cut inequality, and $C$ must be independent of $k$, $G$ and $|V|$. Edges are unweighted. This is the strong thin-tree conjecture; the question requires existence, without an efficient construction or verification algorithm. Goddyn's weaker version permits an arbitrary thinness bound tending to zero with connectivity. It is included here as context, without a separate count or a claim of equivalence. [1, 2]
